meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (root 'чешить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to comb'.
Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'fast'.

examples.trans: We prepare the salads and appetizers quickly.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.trans: We are working as a friendly team all night.
Everyone will get a good bonus!

examples.text: Ну всё понятно с этим кино.
examples.trans: Well, everything is clear with this movie.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: Did someone order a pizza to a restaurant?

examples.text: Туда же переехали и все рестораны.
examples.trans: All the restaurants moved there too.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('I') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: I shaved the coconuts, what is next?
I do not love you very much.
They finished filming a movie with me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'казать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to say', forming an aspectual pair with 'говорить'.
High-frequency Russian pronoun ('something') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.text: Что-то тут у вас очень жарко.
examples.trans: It is somehow very hot in here at your place.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'funny', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: The comedy is truly very funny.
Not a funny movie at all.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('well') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну всё понятно с этим кино.
examples.trans: Well, everything is clear with this movie.
Well yes, that is exactly right.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('yes') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Well yes, that is exactly right.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.

examples.trans: I do not love you very much.
The comedy is truly very funny.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'funny'.

представить.gloss: to imagine, to picture; to introduce

meanings.en: to imagine, to picture; to introduce
meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (root 'ставить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to imagine', forming an aspectual pair with 'представлять'.

examples.text: Представь: тебе сорок лет, жена красавица.
examples.trans: Imagine: you're forty, with a beautiful wife.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'big', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: Senya, hand me the big knife.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'hairbrush', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (root 'ткнуться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to shut up'.

examples.trans: Shut up and do not argue!

examples.text: Заткнись, Вика, я никогда не делаю ошибок!
examples.trans: Shut up, Vika, I never make mistakes!

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We prepare the salads and appetizers quickly.
And it will collect the whole box office.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('not') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I do not love you very much.
We are not going home today.
Let's not get distracted from work.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'порить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to argue', forming an aspectual pair with 'поспорить'.

examples.trans: Shut up and do not argue!
That's a nightmare, I don't argue.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to find', forming an aspectual pair with 'находить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
High-frequency Russian pronoun ('he') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

examples.trans: He is in the kitchen today.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be afraid'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Do not be afraid of a sharp knife.
Instead, be afraid of an ordinary fork!
We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'sharp', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: Do not be afraid of a sharp knife.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Instead, be afraid of an ordinary fork!

examples.text: На столе лежат нож и вилка.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'blow', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
